tEn: Software Engineering After Code Becomes Cheap with Satya Nadella
tZh: 当代码变得廉价后的软件工程——对话萨提亚·纳德拉
sEn: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on why verification, not code generation, becomes the scarce skill in the AI era.
sZh: 微软 CEO 萨提亚·纳德拉谈 AI 时代真正稀缺的不是写代码，而是验证代码。

consensus.en: When code generation becomes cheap, verification becomes the hard part.
consensus.zh: 当代码生成变得廉价，验证就成了难点。

consensus.en: AI-first product building requires rewiring quickly when model jumps happen non-linearly.
consensus.zh: AI 优先的产品构建要求在模型非线性跃迁时快速重构。

consensus.en: Every firm needs control of its own learning loop, context, and harness separate from models.
consensus.zh: 每家公司都需要控制自己的学习循环、上下文和工具链，并与模型分离。

consensus.en: Open-weight models give firms flexibility and are a viable strategy alongside closed models.
consensus.zh: 开放权重模型为企业提供灵活性，是与闭源模型并行的可行策略。

consensus.en: Decision engines are a new primitive for reliable, token-efficient intelligence embedded in software.
consensus.zh: 决策引擎是一种新原语，用于在软件中嵌入可靠、token 高效智能。

consensus.en: Software engineering remains vital; the order of operations and toolchain change, not the value of expertise.
consensus.zh: 软件工程依然至关重要；改变的是操作顺序和工具链，而非专业知识的价值。

contrarian.en: There won't be one frontier model with all knowledge; there should be as many frontier models as firms.
contrarian.zh: 不会有一个掌握所有知识的前沿模型；前沿模型的数量应与企业数量相当。

contrarian.en: Relying on a single AI vendor is a massive strategic mistake; firms must own their AI infrastructure.
contrarian.zh: 依赖单一 AI 供应商是巨大的战略错误；企业必须拥有自己的 AI 基础设施。

contrarian.en: Scaling brings new capabilities but not alignment; we're getting more capable and less reliable.
contrarian.zh: Scaling 带来新能力，但不带来对齐；我们正变得能力更强却更不可靠。

contrarian.en: Treat AI agents as insider risk; separate authority from intelligence architecturally.
contrarian.zh: 将 AI 智能体视为内部风险；在架构上将权限与智能分离。

contrarian.en: The junior hiring slowdown may be temporary as companies reconfigure software factories.
contrarian.zh: 初级招聘放缓可能是暂时的，因为公司正在重构软件工厂。

contrarian.en: IDEs may see a rebirth as decision engines embed intelligence in a token-efficient way.
contrarian.zh: 随着决策引擎以 token 高效的方式嵌入智能，IDE 可能会重生。

turns.zh: 另一方面，我只想把这一点记录下来。我们谈到招聘应届毕业生，所以你仍然在招应届生、初级员工，你在他们身上投资。你看到了这一点，因为很多其他公司和初创公司的一个担忧是，他们放缓甚至停止了招聘，因为他们想，有了 AI，最能高效使用它的人，正如我们之前提到的，是那些有专业知识并能加以利用的人，所以他们非常犹豫招任何刚入职场的人。

turns.en: Great point. So one of the things that we're trying to do is—in this change, this is why I think a little bit of the trends have to be watched carefully over slightly longitudinally versus just one year, because we're in the process of a lot of change. So first job is to make sure internally all of the folks are getting re-orged to places that make sense, like just step one. I mean, even inside of a team, you just want to get the configuration right. Then it makes sense to—oh, what is the industry hire or a new college hire you add to this. And so a little bit of what's happening, I think, is the slowdown, maybe a slowdown to get those quote-unquote new factories of software engineering built, such that new inputs—not just tokens, humans—can come in and then in this new configuration give you a high leverage. I mean, let's face it, what is an AI-native company? They start with a token budget and a human, right? Then they add that person, maxes their token budget, and then says let's add the next human, and then that human gets a token budget, and then their factory gets the budget.
turns.zh: 说得好。我们正在尝试的一件事是——在这个变化中，这就是为什么我认为有些趋势要稍微纵向地、而不只是一年地仔细看，因为我们正处于大量变化的过程中。所以第一件事是确保内部所有人都被重组到合理的位置，这只是第一步。我的意思是，即便在一个团队内部，你也要先把配置弄对。然后才有意义去考虑——哦，行业招聘或新招的大学毕业生，你加进来。所以正在发生的一部分情况，我认为是放缓，也许是放缓来把那些所谓的软件工程新工厂建起来，让新的输入——不只是 token，还有人——能够进来，然后在这个新配置中给你高杠杆。我的意思是，面对现实吧，什么是 AI 原生公司？他们从一份 token 预算和一个人开始，对吧？然后他们加上那个人，用满他的 token 预算，然后说再加下一个人，然后那个人得到一份 token 预算，然后他们的工厂得到预算。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: That is the constructionist way, and it's not like—okay, those companies, if they succeed, they will also be big one day, and they will, and every company is going to start looking like that, and every project team or product team will look like that. And so that process of reconfiguring, new discovery and configuration, it'll take time, and that's where I think trying to draw too many lines as long-term trends, I think it's too early.
turns.zh: 这就是建构主义的方式，并不是说——好吧，那些公司如果成功，有一天也会变大，他们会的，每家公司都会开始看起来像那样，每个项目团队或产品团队都会像那样。所以那个重新配置、新发现和配置的过程需要时间，这就是为什么我认为试图画太多线当作长期趋势，为时过早。

turns.en: Before we get back to the conversation, I'd like to talk about Linear, our season sponsor. Until recently, I was thinking of Linear as a tool that helps plan and organize the work, but it's much more than that. A lot of teams use Linear to ship changes from idea to merge in GitHub, all without leaving the tool. I sat down with Dima, an engineer on the Linear team, to see how devs inside of Linear use Linear to build all of Linear. So here's a real issue.
turns.zh: 在我们回到对话之前，我想谈谈 Linear，我们这一季的赞助商。直到最近，我还把 Linear 看作一个帮助规划和组织工作的工具，但它远不止于此。很多团队用 Linear 把变更从想法一路推进到在 GitHub 合并，全程不离开这个工具。我和 Linear 团队的一位工程师 Dima 坐下来聊了聊，看看 Linear 内部的开发者如何用 Linear 构建整个 Linear。所以这里有个真实的问题。

turns.en: When you submit a review with unsent draft comments, Linear warns you about these comments, but it didn't tell you where those comments were. A customer complained and Dima decided to fix it. But for the fix, Dima did not open his IDE. Instead, he opened up Linear and described the issue to the agent. The agent built a fix, created a PR, and attached Storybook screenshots for easy verification. You can see the fix with the draft comments linked on the screenshot. In the PR, you can open the preview with one click from Linear to play around with the change and see that it worked. And here's my favorite part, guided reviews, which is work in progress. Guided reviews is a new code review experience where the important stuff just pops out. The top of the review has a summary and a diagram of the change. And the pull request is divided into chapters that walk you through what has changed. These blocks highlight the important changes in a way that's easier to understand and review. Oh, and when Dima is finished with all of this, he just self-approves the code and it's merged into GitHub, all without leaving Linear. If you take one thing from this, Linear is no longer just a place for planning tickets and organizing the work. It's where all the work happens: creating the issue, kicking off the agent, checking out the preview, doing the review, and merging to production. Linear is the product development system for teams and AI agents, and I'm loving this evolution. Check it out and get a six-month trial at linear.app/pragmatic.
turns.zh: 当你提交评审时还留着未发送的草稿评论，Linear 会提醒你这些评论的存在，但它不会告诉你这些评论在哪里。有位客户抱怨了这一点，Dima 决定修复它。但为了做这个修复，Dima 并没有打开他的 IDE。相反，他打开 Linear，把问题描述给智能体。智能体构建了修复，创建了 PR，并附上 Storybook 截图以便轻松验证。你可以看到修复效果，草稿评论就链接在截图上。在 PR 里，你可以从 Linear 一键打开预览，亲手试试这个改动，确认它确实生效了。接下来是我最喜欢的部分：引导式评审，目前还在开发中。引导式评审是一种全新的代码评审体验，重要的东西会自己跳出来。评审顶部有摘要和改动示意图。而 PR 被分成若干章节，带你逐步了解改了什么。这些区块以更易理解和评审的方式突出重要改动。哦对了，当 Dima 完成这一切后，他直接自我批准代码，就合并进了 GitHub，全程没有离开 Linear。如果只记住一件事，那就是：Linear 不再只是规划工单、组织工作的地方。它是所有工作发生的地方：创建 issue、启动智能体、查看预览、做评审、合并到生产。Linear 是为团队和 AI 智能体打造的产品开发系统，我很喜欢这个演进。去看看，并在 linear.app/pragmatic 获取六个月试用。

turns.en: If you've ever worked on B2B software, you know how this goes. A customer likes the product, then their security team sends a list: SSO, SCIM provisioning, role-based access. None of it is what you set out to build, but the deal waits on it. WorkOS is the auth infrastructure that covers all of that, so nobody on your team has to debug a customer SAML setup. The newer version of the problem is agents. Once an agent is acting inside of a customer's systems, the enterprise wants to know what it's allowed to do. That's what WorkOS AirLock is for. It's intent-based access control. Most access control only asks who you are. AirLock also asks what the agent is trying to do at the moment it tries to do it. Clear-cut rules like no agent deletes cloud resources run as plain code. For the fuzzier calls, an AI judge evaluates the policy at runtime. You write these policies in plain English and Claude can pull the ones you already had out of Notion and Jira and import them for you. Your agents, whether that's Claude or Devin, connect to a single access point and your MCP servers sit behind it. AirLock is a new layer on top of your existing permissions, so an agent can never get more access than the person who invoked it has. When something risky comes up, AirLock can escalate to a human for approval, say over Slack. The idea is to write the rules once and spend human attention only on the calls that need it. And every request and decision is logged. Visit workos.com/airlock to learn more.
turns.zh: 如果你做过 B2B 软件，你就知道这套流程。客户喜欢这个产品，然后他们的安全团队发来一张清单：SSO、SCIM 预配、基于角色的访问控制。这些都不是你最初想构建的东西，但交易就卡在这上面。WorkOS 是覆盖所有这些的认证基础设施，这样你团队里没人需要去调试客户的 SAML 配置。这个问题的新版本是智能体。一旦智能体在客户的系统里行动，企业就想知道它被允许做什么。这就是 WorkOS AirLock 的用途。它是基于意图的访问控制。大多数访问控制只问你是谁。AirLock 还会问智能体在试图做某事的当下想做什么。像“智能体不得删除云资源”这样明确的规则以普通代码运行。对于更模糊的判断，由 AI 裁判在运行时评估策略。你用自然语言写这些策略，Claude 可以把你在 Notion 和 Jira 里已有的策略拉出来并导入。你的智能体，无论是 Claude 还是 Devin，都连接到一个单一访问点，你的 MCP 服务器位于其后。AirLock 是你现有权限之上的新一层，所以智能体永远无法获得比调用它的人更多的访问权限。当出现风险时，AirLock 可以升级给人类审批，比如通过 Slack。理念是规则写一次，人类注意力只花在真正需要的判断上。而且每个请求和决策都会被记录。访问 workos.com/airlock 了解更多。

turns.en: Now we know whenever anyone is building their software factories, they're changing how they work. A big trend now that we go down to a little bit of the how this is done, a big trend across the industry that I'm seeing and I'm sure you're seeing as well: a lot of tech companies are moving to open models as well. A lot of them are spinning up their inference, or companies like Replicate are buying their inference, they're buying their B200s and just launching the models on it. They all have their own reasons, but from your vantage point, you know, Microsoft is also in the open model serving business with Foundry, for example. How big is this trend and is it inevitable? I'm asking myself, are there parallels to the open source movement and now the open model movement?
turns.zh: 现在我们知道，每当有人在构建他们的软件工厂时，他们都在改变工作方式。现在有一个大趋势，我们稍微深入一点看这是怎么做的——我在整个行业看到的一个大趋势，我相信你也看到了：很多科技公司也在转向开放模型。他们中很多人自己在搭建推理，或者像 Replicate 这样的公司在购买推理，他们买 B200，然后直接在上面部署模型。他们各有各的理由，但从你的视角看，比如微软也在通过 Foundry 做开放模型服务。这个趋势有多大，它是否不可避免？我在问自己，开源运动和现在的开放模型运动之间是否有相似之处？

turns.en: I think that there are for sure the parallels, which is, you know, there's sort of going to be closed models and there'll be competition amongst them, and there will be sort of an alternative to obviously closed, which would be open. Open gives you flexibility. In fact, one of the ways I come at it is with just this: what does the frontier ecosystem look like? It can't be — if you just get past this thing called “there's going to be one frontier model to sort of have all of the world's knowledge,” right? If you don't buy that, right? Then you have to assume that there should be in some sense as many frontier models as firms in the world, right? Because after all, if you go back to actually Hayek, his description of what an economy is, it's all about knowledge being distributed, right? In fact, his entire thing about pricing is a beautiful sort of explanation of, hey, it happens because of knowledge being tacit and distributed throughout the economy. And every firm needs to be in control of it. And if so, then I would even say every firm essentially has both human capital and token capital. So if every firm is going to have both token capital and human capital, the token capital can be an open weight model into which you've embedded your knowledge. That's one. It can also be in the context layer. You could even be using multiple closed models. In fact, collecting even the traces of your usage of those closed models and then using those traces to maybe train a small model on an open weight model for yourself and keeping that combination. When I look at even Copilot, in fact, whether it's GitHub Copilot or Copilot, they're all designed as these multi-model systems, right? In fact, I would say maybe even by the next time you and I talk, everybody would say it's not about even open or closed. Everyone has a model system. In fact, it starts with even a decision engine which says which model to use for what task. And then I have my context and memory and my action space separate from any one model because otherwise you have a complete lock-in. In fact, one of the things I think about is like, wow, if you really got your harness, your model, your memory all coupled, how would you ever get out, right? In fact, what are you doing? And what do you own versus what is owned by the model? Because the model will basically collapse into it everything it sees. And so I think that this dynamic is getting well better understood. Most people again think, oh, this is just some competition amongst tech people. Remember, there's no limit to intelligence. Every bank, every healthcare company, every insurance company, every analyst, everybody needs to sort of have a real thing, architectural approach to figuring out how do they manage to control their own learning and knowledge and have firm differentiation. And in that context, open weight models is one strategy that I think has legs.
turns.zh: 我认为确实有相似之处。也就是说，会有闭源模型，它们之间会有竞争，而闭源显然会有一种替代方案，那就是开放。开放给你灵活性。事实上，我看待这个问题的方式之一就是：前沿生态是什么样子？它不可能是——如果你能接受“最终会有一个前沿模型掌握全世界知识”这个说法，对吧？如果你不信这个，那你就得假设，某种意义上世界上有多少家公司，就该有多少个前沿模型，对吧？因为毕竟，如果你回到哈耶克，他对经济是什么的描述，核心就是知识是分散的，对吧？事实上，他关于价格的整套论述就是一个漂亮的解释：价格之所以出现，是因为知识是隐性的、分散在整个经济中的。而每家公司都需要掌控它。如果是这样，我甚至会说每家公司本质上都同时拥有人力资本和 token 资本。所以如果每家公司都将同时拥有 token 资本和人力资本，那么 token 资本可以是一个开放权重模型，你把你的知识嵌入其中。这是一点。它也可以存在于上下文层。你甚至可以使用多个闭源模型。事实上，收集你使用那些闭源模型的痕迹，然后用这些痕迹在开放权重模型上为你自己训练一个小模型，并保持这种组合。甚至当我看到 Copilot 时，无论是 GitHub Copilot 还是 Copilot，它们都被设计成这种多模型系统，对吧？事实上，我甚至会说，也许下次你我对话时，大家都会说，问题甚至不在于开放还是闭源。每个人都有一个模型系统。事实上，它始于一个决策引擎，决定哪个任务用哪个模型。然后我的上下文、记忆和行动空间都与任何一个模型分离，否则你就被完全锁定了。事实上，我思考的一件事是：哇，如果你真的把你的运行框架、模型、记忆全都耦合在一起，你怎么可能脱身，对吧？事实上，你在做什么？哪些是你拥有的，哪些是模型拥有的？因为模型基本上会把它看到的一切都坍缩进去。所以我认为这种动态正在被更好地理解。大多数人又会想，哦，这只是科技圈的一些竞争。记住，智能是没有上限的。每家银行、每家医疗公司、每家保险公司、每位分析师、每个人都需要有一种真正的、架构性的方法来弄清楚如何控制自己的学习和知识，并实现公司差异化。在这个背景下，开放权重模型是一种我认为有生命力的策略。

turns.en: You know, this is very interesting because I talk with a lot of mid-sized tech company startups and almost all of them are building the things that you just dropped: their own harness, their own context layer, their own context graph, their own inference. And I thought initially, I'm like, well, this kind of makes sense because engineers love to build and if you want to get AI engineering experience, the least risky thing is to build something internal. However, I never thought of this part where it's actually these engineers building for the right reasons, which is the strategic reason or not, they're probably doing their company a service and you're saying that most companies should probably consider owning the system, having replaceable parts primitives because
turns.zh: 你知道，这非常有意思，因为我和很多中型科技公司初创企业交流过，几乎所有的公司都在构建你刚刚提到的那些东西：他们自己的 harness、自己的上下文层、自己的上下文图、自己的推理。我一开始想，这挺合理的，因为工程师喜欢构建，如果你想获得 AI 工程经验，风险最低的事情就是构建一些内部的东西。然而，我从未想过这一部分：实际上这些工程师是出于正确的理由在构建，无论是不是战略理由，他们很可能是在为他们的公司服务，而你说大多数公司可能应该考虑拥有系统，拥有可替换的部件原语，因为

turns.en: Correct. So in fact, what you are observing is correct, which is it's fascinating, right? In fact, I would say if you're a bank, you should check how software companies that are trying to manage in this ecosystem to become frontier are doing it. They're not ceding control. So in some sense, that's what the bank should be doing. So what is the bank in there they will have leverage. So for example, what we have done, you know, what we describe as this IQ layer is we have taken for example the harness that we have underneath co-pilot and GitHub co-pilot, made it a first-class thing that you can now go to foundry as a managed service and you have the harness. So in there, let's say you're building a supply chain system, you can start with our harness just as essentially an open or you can bring Pi or any other open source harness as well in there.
turns.zh: 正确。所以事实上，你观察到的是对的，这很迷人，对吧？事实上，我会说，如果你是一家银行，你应该看看那些试图在这个生态系统中管理以成为前沿的软件公司是如何做的。他们没有放弃控制权。所以从某种意义上说，这就是银行应该做的。那么银行在那里会有什么杠杆？例如，我们所做的，我们描述的这个 IQ 层，就是我们拿来了例如我们在 co-pilot 和 GitHub co-pilot 下面的 harness，把它做成一等公民，你现在可以去 foundry 作为托管服务，你就有了 harness。所以在那里，假设你在构建一个供应链系统，你可以从我们的 harness 开始，本质上就像是一个开放式的，或者你也可以把 Pi 或任何其他开源 harness 带进来。

turns.en: Oh, we love Pi.
turns.zh: 哦，我们喜欢 Pi。

turns.en: But you can just have it like as a managed service, right? So battle tested harness from Microsoft, which we ourselves are using is just available there. And then you can have all the foundry models, right? So you have a harness, you can use multiple models as endpoints, you can have your context layer that is completely separate, right? Your memory and context is yours then. So I think now we have a model system. Oh, by the way, the action space, so with all the plugins and skills and connectors, right? All separate from any given model being only having the visibility to So I think a good sort of classic middle tier platform is emerging even for model first development where you're not just captured and then you can eval everything, right? You can say, hey, I have an eval and my private evals will matter more, right? All these public benchmarks, which by the way is great, but you need to have your own private eval for what is the outcome that matters to you and then look at in your RLE, the real performance for across all these models and continuously optimize. In fact, when I look at even, you know, even with our customers, they start with a frontier model. Then they say, well, great, I've got all those traces. Now I'm going to flip to, hey, this is a deterministic workflow. I mean, it's not like I don't need the next big model drop. I want to now cost optimize. I'll drop, you know, an MAI flash model, drop it in there, use the traces to fine tune it and there you have it. So therefore that's all stuff you can do in foundry. So that type of work, I think is what's going to increasingly be true.
turns.zh: 但你可以把它作为托管服务来用，对吧？所以来自微软的久经考验的 harness，我们自己也在用，就在那里可用。然后你可以拥有所有 foundry 模型，对吧？所以你有一个 harness，你可以使用多个模型作为端点，你可以有一个完全独立的上下文层，对吧？那么你的记忆和上下文就是你的了。所以我认为现在我们有了一个模型系统。哦，顺便说一下，动作空间，所以所有的插件、技能和连接器，对吧？都与任何给定的模型分开，只有可见性。所以我认为一个好的经典中间层平台正在出现，即使对于模型优先的开发也是如此，你不仅仅是被捕获，然后你可以评估一切，对吧？你可以说，嘿，我有一个评估，我的私有评估更重要，对吧？所有这些公共基准，顺便说一下，这很好，但你需要有自己的私有评估，针对对你重要的结果，然后在你的 RLE 中查看所有模型的真实性能并持续优化。事实上，当我看到甚至我们的客户，他们从前沿模型开始。然后他们说，太好了，我有了所有这些轨迹。现在我要转向，嘿，这是一个确定性工作流。我的意思不是我不需要下一个大模型发布。我现在想要成本优化。我会放入一个 MAI flash 模型，放进去，使用轨迹对其进行微调，然后就有了。所以所有这些你都可以在 foundry 中做。所以这类工作，我认为会越来越普遍。

turns.en: We're saying that's you're already seeing that a lot of companies have the reinforcement learning environment as well on top of the evals so that they can stay in control, control pricing, and also I guess not leak their business data to some of the AI companies that might want to train their models on it, right?
turns.zh: 我们是说，你已经看到很多公司在评估之上也有强化学习环境，这样他们可以保持控制、控制定价，而且我猜也不会把业务数据泄露给一些可能想用这些数据训练模型的 AI 公司，对吧？

turns.en: So if you think about it, right? So the way the simple analogy I have least my head is, you know, people, you know, in the past, whether you know, in an insurance company, in a bank, in a healthcare company said, hey, I'm going to get a relational database. Great. I'm going to deploy a relational database. On top of it, I may even buy some software that runs on that relational database that is sort of comes with its own business logic.
